name: Mark Carney
description: Canadian prime minister assessed through his programme of economic investment, social protection and national sovereignty.

axes.brief: He sought an electoral mandate and a parliamentary government with institutional accountability and delegated expert administration.
axes.counterEvidence: Central-bank experience supports professional delegation but does not establish rejection of elections or parliamentary removal.

axes.brief: The programme combines firearms restrictions, additional police capacity and protections against hate with civil rights and due process.
axes.counterEvidence: Security funding does not establish endorsement of unlimited tracking, indefinite detention or censorship of ordinary institutional criticism.

qualifications.4: Existing legal personal choices and public-health limits coexist; a general unrestricted drug-use claim extends beyond his programme.
qualifications.6: Crime prevention and privacy place conflicting demands on storing nonsuspects’ movements for years.
qualifications.14: Accountability and protection of confidential information conflict when disclosure procedures are unspecified.

axes.brief: His programme recognises Indigenous cultures, French-language identity and Canada’s plural society while strengthening a shared Canadian public culture.
axes.counterEvidence: Promoting Canadian content and francophone migration qualifies cultural neutrality; plural identities do not override all common institutions.

qualifications.16: Shared participation and preservation of distinct identities both receive explicit support, with neither an exclusive integration goal.

axes.brief: He proposed reduced immigration totals linked to capacity while maintaining lawful skills, family and humanitarian pathways.
axes.counterEvidence: Capacity-based restrictions differ from racial or blanket cultural exclusion; removals of failed asylum claims follow process.

axes.brief: Expanded defence investment and domestic defence industry support credible deterrence and cooperation with allies.
axes.counterEvidence: Strategic autonomy is not a general permission for aggressive war; negotiated diplomacy and defence capability remain concurrent objectives.

qualifications.5: Protecting sovereignty supports defensive action, but the programme does not restrict every possible mission solely to responding to an attack.
qualifications.14: Deterrence and avoiding escalation are both important; neither universally takes precedence.

axes.brief: He defends Canadian sovereignty against US pressure while supporting negotiated international cooperation and diversified trade.
axes.counterEvidence: Retaining a national currency and sovereign border administration coexist with alliances and agreed international rules.

qualifications.3: Domestic constitutional authority and treaty obligations can conflict; no categorical ordering of every international court case is established.

axes.brief: The programme retains a mainly privately owned economy with public broadcasting, public infrastructure and a federal affordable-housing agency.
axes.counterEvidence: Public investment and procurement should not be mistaken for public ownership of every recipient firm or of all natural resources.

qualifications.8: Public financing institutions and private banking coexist, but the programme does not establish a general commercial public-bank commitment.

axes.brief: He combines trade diversification and open internal commerce with Canadian procurement, strategic resilience and retaliatory tariffs.
axes.counterEvidence: Retaliation against the US does not demonstrate opposition to all international trade; preferences differ for strategic goods and ordinary commerce.

axes.brief: Private market production is combined with targeted industrial investment, competition policy and major public projects.
axes.counterEvidence: Directed public spending does not constitute ordinary compulsory production quotas; his former central-bank role qualifies political direction of monetary policy.

qualifications.6: Cost-of-living relief and competitive pricing coexist; subsidies are not generally mandatory essential-goods price ceilings.

axes.brief: Targeted benefits and fair taxation coexist with middle-income tax reductions and growth-oriented investment.
axes.counterEvidence: This is not an unconditional tax-and-transfer equalisation programme; no general inheritance, wealth or land transfer programme is established.

qualifications.4: Basic protection and meaningful participation both matter, making a restriction to a minimal safety net too narrow.
qualifications.9: Fairness supports sharing burdens but a broad accumulated-wealth transfer tax is not an explicit policy.
qualifications.10: Spending restraint and sufficient benefits pull in opposite directions.

axes.brief: Policy is articulated through civil institutions and public purposes rather than approval by Catholic authorities.
axes.counterEvidence: Personal Catholic faith and inherited public traditions are distinct from religious control of legislation.

qualifications.11: Public neutrality and inherited cultural symbols can coexist; a categorical removal requirement is stronger than the documented programme.

axes.brief: The platform protects equal citizenship and reproductive and sexual-minority rights while accommodating cultural continuity.
axes.counterEvidence: Liberal rights commitments do not imply that every tradition must change immediately or that historical customs have no value.

qualifications.14: Reform and predictable institutions both matter under a broad gradualism rule.
qualifications.16: Inherited culture can be valued without making preservation unconditional.

axes.brief: His programme promotes faster major-project decisions, AI investment and technology-led growth, with environmental and medical safeguards.
axes.counterEvidence: Technology support is more direct than his position on irreversible neurological or embryo enhancements, which remain uncertain extrapolations.

qualifications.11: Personal choice and irreversible neurological risk give opposing considerations beyond the infrastructure programme.
qualifications.13: Research innovation and embryo ethical concerns are both plausible; no specific enhancement endorsement is documented.

axes.brief: He proposes a more integrated national economy through cooperation with provinces, territories and Indigenous governing bodies.
axes.counterEvidence: Federal coordination does not abolish provincial constitutional responsibilities or establish one central police authority.

qualifications.14: Common economic rules and provincial tax autonomy both have weight; tax competition is not specifically prohibited.

axes.brief: Education, inclusion and opportunity support a qualified account of socially learned behaviour alongside individual biological variation.
axes.counterEvidence: The programme supplies contextual evidence, not a quantified theory of the inherited and learned causes of every psychological trait.

religion.reason: The biography identifies him as a practising Catholic; identity is separated from the civil foundations of policy.
